n: In June 1829 the translation moved to the Peter Whitmer Sr. farm in Fayette, New York. David Whitmer, who had helped bring Joseph and Oliver there, asks what he should do and hears the familiar opening words.
David is told to pay close attention to God’s word, which is living and penetrating.

f.w: the dividing asunder of both joints and marrow
f.g: an image of God’s word cutting to the innermost part of a person.

n: The harvest image calls David to labor while there is still daylight — while life and opportunity last.
Desire and willingness to work are what make David “called of God.”
The promise of answered prayer is repeated to David.

f.w: if you will knock it shall be opened unto you

n: David is to help build Zion and keep all the commandments.
Obedience and enduring to the end lead to eternal life, the greatest of all God’s gifts.

f.w: eternal life, which gift is the greatest of all the gifts of God

n: If David asks the Father in faith, he will receive the Holy Ghost to help him testify of what he will hear and see — a hint that he would become one of the Three Witnesses.

f.w: stand as a witness of the things of which you shall both hear and see

f.g: gives the ability to speak, providing the words.

n: Christ identifies himself as Creator of heaven and earth — a light that cannot be hidden.

f.w: who created the heavens and the earth
a light which cannot be hid in darkness

n: The fulness of the gospel will come forth through the Gentiles to the house of Israel — the reverse of its first spread, as Book of Mormon prophecy foretold.

f.w: from the Gentiles unto the house of Israel

n: David is called to assist; if faithful, he will be blessed spiritually and temporally. He later testified of the plates for the rest of his life, though he separated from the Church in 1838.

f.g: in matters of the spirit and in practical, earthly life.
